title: Two heirs in a year
hookLine: his son Kharak Singh sickened and died, and his grandson Nau Nihal Singh was killed by a falling arch

cards: A young prince walks back from his father's cremation, through a gateway in Lahore. He's strong, clever, already a commander, the heir the court was watching.
Mourners walk with him, the smoke of the pyre still in their clothes. Overhead, stones shift. The archway comes down, and the prince is struck.
The kingdom that looked so solid has cremated one king that morning, and now its heir is down among the fallen stones.

teach.h: KHARAK SINGH TAKES THE THRONE AND FALLS ILL.
teach.b: Kharak Singh, the Maharaja's eldest son, took the throne. Histories describe him as gentle and not suited to the hard politics of the court.
Power slipped quickly into other hands, among them his own son's and the ministers'. His favorite adviser was killed, and later Kharak Singh himself fell ill and died.
Some at the time suspected poison; nobody can say for certain.

teach.h: NAU NIHAL SINGH AND THE FALLING ARCH.
teach.b: His son, Nau Nihal Singh, was young, able and ambitious, already ruling in all but name. On the day of his father's cremation, as he passed under a gateway, part of it fell and struck him, and he died of his injuries.
Histories record the suspicion that it was no accident. Some point to the ministers who gained from his death, and say the story of the hours after was kept close. Others say the arch simply fell.
The sources don't settle it, and i won't pretend they do.

teach.h: A KINGDOM HANGING BY A THREAD.
teach.b: The Maharaja had spent a lifetime building a kingdom.

Within a short time of his death, his son and grandson were both gone, and the throne was open to whoever could seize it. A kingdom can look like a fortress and still hang by a thread, or by the stones of one gateway.

how: Sikhs meet the deaths of Kharak Singh and Nau Nihal Singh in histories of the years after Maharaja Ranjit Singh, when the Lahore throne passed quickly from hand to hand.

games.q: you're a young prince returning from your father's cremation. the court's eyes are on you. you pass under a gateway. what happens, as histories tell it?
o: part of the gateway falls and strikes you.
you leave Lahore for the hills.
games.why: the arch came down on Nau Nihal Singh, and he died of his injuries. whether it was an accident is still argued.

practice: Think of one kind of power you hold, a role in your family, money, health, influence over someone, and picture honestly, without fear, how it could be gone tomorrow.
Then ask what would still be there if it went, and rest in that, breath by breath. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.

carryVoice: Your line: power is fragile. A throne is only as steady as the people around it. Day nine hundred twenty-six, done.
